text.tspan: 115 laps at Thunderhill West across five
track days, logged on two apps that
disagree with each other. The interesting
part wasn't building the chart. It was
redesigning it a year later and finding
what I'd let slide because I already knew
Each mark is one lap. The heavy line under
each track day is that day's
— my fastest sectors, strung together. The
floor: pace I'd already proven in pieces but
The gap between floor and cluster is the
honest measure. Not "am I faster?" — that
flatters you, because tyres and weather and
traffic all move. It's "how close am I to the lap

g.aria-label: Scatter plot of 115 lap times across five track days, with a theoretical-best floor line beneath each day. Times improve from about 1:39 to 1:28.

text.tspan: Hover or focus a lap for detail
MATCH THE PUBLISHED DASHBOARD, NOT MEASURED.
ANCHORED TO ITS REAL FIGURES: 115 LAPS, 16
scattered high cluster, topping out at 2:01.14, nearly
forty seconds off pace. The track dried through the
afternoon and I set my best, 1:28.39, on lap 112.
Same day, same car, same driver.
The original is still on Tableau Public. A
serviceable chart; I was pleased with it.
Coming back cold, I could see where I'd
designed for someone who already knew the
answer — which is to say, for me.
A teal dot and a purple dot, unlabelled. I knew which
was which. Nobody else did. Now they say
Marks the size of the story
Large opaque circles buried the early sessions in one
blob. Smaller marks with some transparency let
Callouts drew rules straight through the plot. Detail
now sits in a readout below, so nothing is drawn over
It read 95s, 100s, 105s. Nobody at a track day talks
, and the x-axis is split by
track day instead of an unlabelled run.
None of it is dramatic. That's the point — it's
the ordinary maintenance a chart needs when
it stops being something you made and
caught it by treating my own work as
season, almost none of it in one leap. The
theoretical-best floor drops steadily, and the
cluster follows at a lag. I could always drive
the sectors before I could drive the lap.
The wet session is the most useful thing here,
and I nearly filtered it out for being ugly. Forty
seconds of penalty on the same day I set my
best time argues about context better than
